findings.title: Data race on `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` in `searchSupport.init` worker goroutines
findings.body: In `searchSupport.init`, each `group.Go` closure increments `totalBatchesIndexed++` and assigns to the outer `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) before returning `err`, while the parent goroutine also assigns `err = group.Wait()`. Previously, `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu.Lock()` for its entire execution, largely serializing these workers. With the lock narrowed to the final cache assignment, `s.build` now executes concurrently across `s.initWorkers` goroutines, causing data races on both `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` (and allowing a `nil` result from one worker to overwrite a non-nil `err` in another worker before `return err` is evaluated). Use a local ` _, _, err := s.build(...)` inside the closure and an `atomic.Int64` (or `len(stats)`) for `totalBatchesIndexed`.

findings.title: Unsynchronized `b.cache` read in `TotalDocs` and unguarded concurrent `BuildIndex` for the same key
findings.body:
Narrowing `b.cacheMu.Lock()` in `BuildIndex` to only guard `b.cache[key] = idx` introduces two concurrency issues:
1. `TotalDocs()` (lines 144-154, now called in `search.go:216` after the `WatchWriteEvents` goroutine has already started) iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. If a watch event or search request triggers `BuildIndex` concurrently, Go will panic with a concurrent map iteration and map write error.
2. When `getOrCreateIndex` encounters a cache miss concurrently for the same `NamespacedResource` (e.g. from concurrent `Search` calls or `handleEvent`), multiple goroutines will now run `BuildIndex` for the same `key` simultaneously. For file-backed indexes (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), the second `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` call on the same path will fail; for in-memory indexes, the second build will overwrite `b.cache[key]` and drop any writes applied to the first instance.

findings.title: Postgres integration test fails in Drone due to hardcoded `localhost` in `addStorageServerToConfig`
findings.body: `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` only started failing on Postgres with this PR because `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` at startup, whereas previously the test never made any gRPC calls and therefore never connected to the `resource_api` database. In `addStorageServerToConfig` (lines 75-80), the `postgres` branch hardcodes `db_host` to `"localhost"` instead of reading the host and credentials from `cfg.Raw.GetSection("database")` like the MySQL branch does, which fails in Drone where Postgres runs in a separate service container. Parsing the Postgres connection config instead of skipping the test preserves integration test coverage for Postgres startup.

findings.title: Context leak on `NewResourceServer` init failure and unread `s.initErr` after `Stop`
findings.body: In `NewResourceServer`, `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` is created on line 229, but if `s.Init(ctx)` fails on line 258, `cancel()` is not called before returning the error, leaking the context and any background goroutines started prior to the failure (such as the watcher goroutine if `s.initWatcher()` fails after `s.search.init(ctx)`). Additionally, removing `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil` from all RPC handlers means the `s.initErr` assignments in `Stop()` (`"service is stopping"` / `"service is stopped"`) are never checked, so RPC methods will no longer reject requests once `Stop()` has been called.
